title: Triangular Merger: Which EIN Survives the Reverse Flip
scenario_text: Inconel Dynamics licenses software to a customer that just restructured, and RevOps must decide which legal entity carries the renewal for tax reporting. Three NetSuite records exist. C-4001 is "Kovar Analytics, Inc." (EIN 45-2210881, Delaware, the historical contracting party since 2020). C-4002 is "Kovar Holdings, Inc." (EIN 82-6640190, Delaware, incorporated 2024-02-01). C-4003 is "Kovar Merger Sub, Inc." (EIN 88-1120774, incorporated 2024-02-01, no operating history). The customer's counsel sent a closing memo dated 2024-03-15: to complete a venture financing, Kovar Holdings was formed as a new parent, and Kovar Merger Sub merged WITH AND INTO Kovar Analytics, with Kovar Analytics surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Holdings (a reverse triangular merger). The memo states expressly: "The operating company, Kovar Analytics, Inc., survives the merger and retains its EIN 45-2210881; Merger Sub ceases to exist; all contracts of the operating company remain in force without assignment." D&B updated the family tree to show Holdings as domestic ultimate parent. The customer's AP portal now shows invoices should be addressed to "Kovar Holdings, Inc." A revenue analyst, seeing the AP portal and the new parent, proposes moving the subscription to the Holdings record (EIN 82-6640190) and retiring the Analytics record. Legal notes no assignment agreement was ever executed for the license, and the surviving-entity language means the original contract counterparty is unchanged even though the corporate parent above it is new. A refreshed W-9 arrived listing Kovar Analytics, Inc. under its unchanged EIN 45-2210881, yet the customer's Coupa procurement portal, edited by a separate accounts-payable team, still shows Kovar Holdings, Inc. as bill-to. The renewal quote is due in five days, and the analyst must reconcile the portal's bill-to instruction against both the closing memo's surviving-entity language and the newly filed W-9 before the order form is generated, because an invoice to the wrong EIN will be rejected by the customer's tax team.
question: Which entity is the authoritative contracting party for the renewal, and under which EIN should the license invoices be issued?
choices: Kovar Holdings, Inc. (EIN 82-6640190), because it is now the domestic ultimate parent and the AP portal directs invoices to it.
Kovar Analytics, Inc. (EIN 45-2210881), which survived the reverse triangular merger, retained its EIN, and remains the contracting party with no assignment executed.
Kovar Merger Sub, Inc. (EIN 88-1120774), because the merger sub is the vehicle that effected the transaction and absorbs the contracts.
A new combined entity under EIN 82-6640190, since a merger always creates a successor taxpayer that inherits the subsidiary's contracts.
